One row per grid connection, solar plant and battery. Energy meters in kWh or Wh, archived with the aggregation "Counter"; the current power in W or kW is optional. House consumption = grid import + solar production + battery discharge − grid export − battery charge. Without solar and battery a grid row with the import is enough.

Optional for costs in euros: the electricity price as an archived variable in ct/kWh or €/kWh (for a dynamic tariff the current price, for example from Tibber) and the feed-in tariff. The costs count working costs only, without base fee.
Requests of the assistants that did not reach everything, newest first. The last 50 are kept.

Every request as a line in a file in the log directory of Symcon. After 24 hours or the number of lines a new file starts and the previous one is kept, so one to two days are available. Tokens and pairing codes are never written.

elements.caption: Hint for scripts and AI assistants: HAGT_QueryState(int $InstanceID, string $Room, string $Type, string $Name, bool $ActiveOnly): string returns the same text as the tool get_state (first line = count, then room | name | type | state). $Type is one of light, switch, socket, appliance, blind, thermostat, media, humidifier, fan, window, door, presence, water_leak, temperature, humidity, air_quality, measurement, meter. Empty parameters mean no restriction. The property Accesses is a JSON list of accesses, one per assistant: Name, Token, DefaultRoom, ReadOnly, InPath. Each assistant logs in with its own token as Authorization: Bearer <token>; with InPath the endpoint also accepts that token without Authorization header at <hook path>/<token>. Home Assistant (MCP integration) only works with InPath. Other assistants such as ChatGPT, Codex or Claude Code use their own token, in the header or with InPath in the address. The Claude app signs in with OAuth: a custom connector with the Connect address from the instance Connect Control (or another public HTTPS address) followed by the hook path, without a token, and HAGT_CreatePairingCode for the pairing code; it needs neither InPath nor the token. An access without a token gets one on apply (64 hex characters); a token set by script needs at least 24 characters. An access with ReadOnly only gets the tool get_state. DefaultRoom applies when a tool call names neither room nor name nor floor; room=all then means the whole house. The script functions have no access and therefore no default room. The property Rooms is an optional JSON list (Name, Aliases, Floor) that gives rooms aliases and a floor; with floors the tools also accept the parameter floor. Room names are the words the user speaks (Küche, Bad oben), without technical additions. Each room name may appear only once; an alias may belong to several rooms, room= then means all of them. The Room of a device is a room of the room list or empty; the form names rooms that are missing there. The property Devices is a JSON list of devices with their capabilities: Room, Name, Aliases, Type, Invert, ReadOnly (true = the assistant may query the device but not switch it), StateVariableID (state or measured value; for a thermostat the current temperature), LevelVariableID (brightness or position) and SetpointVariableID (setpoint of a thermostat). Each type needs at least one of these fields: light StateVariableID or LevelVariableID, blind LevelVariableID, window StateVariableID or LevelVariableID, thermostat SetpointVariableID, appliance StateVariableID or PowerVariableID, media StateVariableID, PlaybackVariableID or VolumeVariableID, humidifier StateVariableID or SetpointVariableID, fan StateVariableID or FanVariableID, meter EnergyVariableID, all other types StateVariableID; an ID of 0 or 1 means not set. A missing key counts as 0; the columns ending in Label are filled by the form, a script may leave them out. The type meter (a sub-distribution, wallbox or flat meter) needs EnergyVariableID and never counts in a device total. MeteredBy is the EnergyVariableID of the meter above a device or meter (0 = none); the answers name per meter what is measured below it and the rest. A heat pump (type appliance) can also have HeatVariableID (heat meter archived as counter, never in an electricity total) and HeatPowerVariableID (heat output); the answers then name the heat, the performance factor over a period and the COP now. The energy balance is the property Sources, a JSON list with one row per grid connection, solar plant or battery: Type (grid, solar or battery), Name, EnergyIn and EnergyOut (energy meters archived as counters: grid import and export, solar production, battery discharge and charge), PowerIn and PowerOut (the current power in the same order) and Invert. Solar only has EnergyIn and PowerIn. A single signed power in PowerIn counts negative as export or charging, Invert reverses it; HAGT_RunSelfTest shows how the current value counts. The older properties GridImportVariableID and so on are moved into Sources on apply. HAGT_UISourceForm(int $InstanceID, string $Type, int $PowerOut) names the fields of each type; 0 is enough for PowerOut. PriceVariableID (electricity price, archived, in ct/kWh or €/kWh; a suffix containing ct or Cent means cents, ct alone is enough, with € or EUR euros, otherwise values above 2 count as cents) and FeedInTariff (ct/kWh) add costs in euros. The fields of each type (volume, mode, fan and others) are named by HAGT_UIDeviceForm(int $InstanceID, string $Type, string $Room, int $MeteredBy); '' and 0 are enough for Room and MeteredBy. The name of each field is its key in the rows of Devices (for example PowerVariableID, EnergyVariableID, MeteredBy). air_quality is for CO2, VOC, particulate matter and air quality indices, measurement for every other value such as brightness or pressure. A smoke detector is measurement. Power, also a heat output, counts in mW, W, kW or MW (without a unit W); energy meters and heat meters count in mWh, Wh, kWh or MWh (without a unit kWh) and are archived as counters. Any other unit does not count. The volume counts in percent of the range of the variable, also for a range in dB (-80 to 18 dB: 50 % = -31 dB), and is sent in the step size of the variable. For every blind HAGT_RunSelfTest shows which value counts as open; if open and closed are swapped, set Invert. window, door, presence and water_leak count as active (open, detected) when the value is true or above 0, with Invert only when it is false or 0; a window contact with 0 closed, 1 tilted and 2 open thus counts as open from 1. HAGT_UIDeviceForm and HAGT_UIDeviceChanged only serve the edit dialog of this list, HAGT_UIImportAlexa opens a window with devices proposed from an Alexa instance, HAGT_UISetAlexaTakes ticks all or none of them, HAGT_UIApplyAlexa releases the ticked ones. The assistant has three tools: get_state, set_state (command on, off, open, close, stop, or percent, or temperature in °C for a thermostat; only what a released device can do is offered, and devices of a group that do not understand a command are left out) and run_scene. Depending on the released devices set_state also offers humidity, mode, fan_speed, color_temperature, color, volume, volume_change and mute, and the commands play, pause, next and previous. Clients that show MCP Apps, such as the Claude app, also get show_chart (history, consumption and the energy balance as charts) and show_devices (device cards with switches and sliders, operated through control_device, which only the cards see). HAGT_SwitchDevices(int $InstanceID, string $Room, string $Type, string $Name, bool $On): string switches the matching devices on or off, HAGT_SetLevel(int $InstanceID, string $Room, string $Type, string $Name, float $Percent): string sets brightness or position in percent (0 switches a light off; blinds and windows: 0 = closed, 100 = open). Both need at least one filter, a name must match exactly one device, and they return one line per device with the result. HAGT_RunScene(int $InstanceID, string $Room, string $Name): string starts exactly one scene of the scene list (empty name = nothing is started, the answer lists the scenes; the room may stay empty). HAGT_GetEndpoint(int $InstanceID): string returns the hook path. HAGT_GetAddresses(int $InstanceID, string $AccessName): string names the addresses of an access (empty name = all accesses) with <token> as a placeholder; no script function returns a token. HAGT_ExportConfiguration(int $InstanceID): string returns all properties as JSON, lists as lists and every token as <token> (an empty token stays empty); no other function reads Accesses without tokens. Properties are written with IPS_SetProperty(int $InstanceID, string $Name, mixed $Value), a list as JSON text, and take effect with IPS_ApplyChanges(int $InstanceID). HAGT_AddAccess(int $InstanceID, string $Name, bool $ReadOnly, bool $InPath, string $DefaultRoom): string adds an access without a token and applies it; the module then creates the token. A script that does not know the tokens adds accesses this way and never writes Accesses itself. HAGT_RunSelfTest(int $InstanceID): string checks accesses, lists and endpoint without side effects (first line OK or ERROR). Status 104 = no access yet (a new access gets its token on Apply), 201 = the room list has errors or no access is free of errors (the form marks the rows red); a faulty access, device or scene, for example with a deleted variable, only disables itself, the energy balance only as a whole. Sign-in with OAuth (offered as soon as Symcon Connect is active): HAGT_CreatePairingCode(int $InstanceID, string $AccessName): string returns a six-digit pairing code for an access, valid for 10 minutes; the user enters it on the sign-in page of the assistant, which then gets the rights of that access.
